hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Zero builds: re-read the register census in the superseded record's `verification` field. It already reports that ours materialises the base at 3 sites (@0x22c, @0x5cc, @0x10e0) while the target materialises it at 10, and that r19 is the cache copied by the two `mr`. If the j-loop loads at +0xef8/+0xfd4 read their base from r31 rather than from r19 in BOTH streams -- which the aligned view in this record shows they do, `add r4,r31,r3` against `addi r0,r3,3368` / `lwzx r0,r31,r0` -- then the j-loops never touch the cached register at all and the coupling premise is refuted before the first build. READ THAT FIRST: this record states the hypothesis honestly but its own aligned-view evidence already points against it, and a lane that opens with the census will not spend a probe on it.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no - and the caveat is recorded deliberately. The coupling is inferred from the CO-OCCURRENCE of the two components across five forms over two runs (probes G/I/J of the superseded record and probe A here all reach 12t together), not from any target-side evidence that one causes the other. Correlation across forms that all destroy the same web is weak evidence for coupling and equally consistent with both components simply being sensitive to the same web for independent reasons.
hypothesis.statement: The two ours-only `mr` at +0x5d8/+0x670 and the twin j-loop addressing pair are ONE coupled allocator decision, not two residuals, and the coupling is the `r19` long-lived base cache. Every form that removes the cache (probe A here, probes G/I/J of the superseded record) closes the j-loop addressing pair and simultaneously costs elsewhere, landing in the same fuzzy-rejected 12t basin; every form that keeps the cache keeps both `mr` copies AND the indexed j-loop load. No probe in three runs has ever separated them. The untried work is to test the coupling DIRECTLY rather than through the j-loop: force the base cache to die between the two `mr` sites without touching the j-loops at all -- e.g. by introducing an intervening use of potionicon_tab spelled through a different expression in the region between +0x5d8 and +0x670 -- and read whether the j-loop clusters at +0xef8/+0xfd4 move as a side effect. If they move, the residual is ONE mechanism and the 12t basin is its floor; if they do not, the coupling hypothesis is dead and the two components are independently workable.
